name: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk

frontmatter.title: GoTo: a profitable platform trading below its own cash
frontmatter.summary: GoTo has turned profitable, raised its adjusted EBITDA guidance once in 2026, and now sits on net cash and stakes worth more than its market capitalisation. We initiate at Buy: the operating business is being valued at close to nothing while fintech compounds and ride-hailing absorbs the cap.
thesis: Three consecutive quarters of net profit and a single guidance raise in 2026 mark the end of the cash-burn era; 9M2026 EBITDA was already at a double-digit margin, so FY2026E is anchored on actuals, not hope.
Fintech is the growth engine: 3Q26 net revenue growth of roughly half year on year and adjusted EBITDA more than quadrupled, with FY2026 guidance raised once to the revised range.

On-demand services is the regulated part: the two-wheel cap cost the company a material amount of EBITDA in 2026 and ODS EBITDA still grew year on year in 3Q26, which is the evidence the franchise can absorb it.
The balance sheet is the margin of safety: net cash plus investments exceed the market capitalisation, so the market is paying nothing for a business now generating cash.
Capital returns are real but not a dividend story: cash bought back, treasury shares cancelled, and a further authorisation running to June 2027.
Bear case is regulatory: implementing rules for delivery could widen the commission cap and fintech credit costs are unproven through a cycle.

catalysts.event: FY2026 results and first FY2027 guidance; confirmation of the revised group range adjusted EBITDA landing zone
Implementing regulations for delivery services from the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs
End of the current buyback authorisation

blocks.text: **BUY · target Rp53 · 120.8% from Rp24.** We initiate coverage of GoTo Gojek Tokopedia at Buy. The company reported its third consecutive quarter of net profit in 3Q26 — net profit of IDR441.0bn — on net revenue of IDR5,600.0bn and group adjusted EBITDA of IDR950.0bn [S2]. It has raised FY2026 guidance once in 2026, to IDR3,500.0bn at the low end for the group and IDR1,900.0bn at the low end for fintech [S2].

The variant view is not that GoTo is a good platform. It is that the market is currently paying almost nothing for the platform at all. Market capitalisation is IDR25,597.5bn at Rp24 [S0], against 3Q26 cash and investment holdings that together exceed the market capitalisation [S4]. Net of debt, the enterprise value the market assigns is a small fraction of one year of net revenue. Our weighted blend of the DCF and the EV/sales cross-check values the equity at Rp45 per share — the standalone DCF is Rp50 and the EV/sales leg Rp38 — or Rp53 after the twelve-month roll; at the current price the market capitalisation is below the cash plus associate stakes carried on the balance sheet, before the operating business is counted [S4]. What moves the value is the durability of the fintech margin, whether the commission cap widens to delivery, and the terminal multiple the market will pay for an Indonesian platform.

Platform economics in Indonesia are a share-of-transaction business: the platform keeps a commission on rides, food and payments, and the fixed cost of the app is spread over a very large user base. The market has historically priced these names on transaction value rather than earnings, which is why a profitable quarter can coexist with a depressed share price for a while.

GoTo is the holding company of Gojek (on-demand mobility, food delivery and logistics) and GoPay/GoTo Financial (payments, consumer lending, merchant services), plus an e-commerce service-fee relationship with Tokopedia following the 2024 transaction in which Tokopedia was deconsolidated [S3]. The group reports three views of the same base: gross transaction value of 685.6tn in FY2025, annual transacting users of 72.5m users, and net revenue of IDR18,322.0bn in FY2025 [S3][S2].

Three segments carry the P&L. On-demand services earns a take rate on rides, food and logistics; its adjusted EBITDA ran IDR464.0bn in 2Q26 and IDR347.0bn in 3Q26 — about a quarter lower quarter on quarter, the first full quarter under the two-wheel cap, and still marginally above the year-earlier quarter [S5 p.20][S5 p.32]. Fintech earns interchange, lending and merchant fees on a payments and credit book; 3Q26 net revenue grew strongly and fintech adjusted EBITDA reached IDR550.0bn in 3Q26 against IDR950.0bn for the group, and FY2026 guidance was raised once, to IDR1,900.0bn at the low end [S5][S2]. E-commerce is now a service fee rather than a consolidated marketplace: IDR235.0bn in 3Q26 [S2].

The strategy since 2024 has been to stop buying growth. Management closed Vietnam in September 2024, deconsolidated Tokopedia, and shifted to a mass-market product with lower average order values — a trade-off it describes openly, with mobility adjusted EBITDA margin compressed in 3Q26, down year on year, "entirely due to the cap" [S6]. The founder and early-investor group retains control, with a free float of 64.6% [S0]; the data pack's insider and institutional fields overlap and sum above the free float, so we cite only the float.

The shape of the company is best understood as a two-sided consumer platform monetised through three segments. On-demand services is the original Gojek business — two-wheel and four-wheel rides, food delivery, parcel and freight logistics — earning a take rate on every transaction; it has the deepest driver network and is where the regulator has intervened most directly, because the people who supply the service are the people the regulation protects [S7]. Fintech is GoPay and GoTo Financial: the wallet, merchant payment processing, consumer lending through the paylater and cash-loan products, and merchant services; it is the fastest-growing segment by revenue and the one whose guidance has moved up once in 2026 [S2][S5]. E-commerce is no longer a consolidated marketplace: after the Tokopedia transaction the group books a service fee, a high-margin, capital-light line that no longer drags consolidated losses [S3][S2]. Strategy since 2024 has been to stop buying growth — Vietnam closed, Tokopedia deconsolidated, a mass-market product with lower average order values that management says widens the addressable market and defends share at the cost of revenue per order [S6]. The footprint is overwhelmingly Indonesian, with the mobility and delivery network concentrated in dense urban corridors and the wallet used well beyond the platform's own transactions [S3]. Competitively GoTo is a co-leader with Grab in rides and food but a challenger in lending, where bank-owned and digital lenders are larger — the mature segment is the one under regulatory pressure and the growing one is the one where the group is sub-scale [S3][S5].

Indonesian on-demand and digital payments is a two-large-platform market: GoTo on the Gojek/GoPay side and Grab on the Grab/OVO side, with Shopee's ecosystem and DANA contesting payments and e-commerce [S3]. GoTo's own disclosure puts annual transacting users at 72.5m users, up year on year [S2], and the group processed IDR685.6tn of gross transaction value in FY2025 [S3].

The regulatory reset is the defining industry event of 2026. Presidential Regulation on transport-worker protection caps the platform commission on two-wheel transport at 8.0%, effective July 2026, and extends rule-making to food and goods delivery through the Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs [S7][S2]. GoTo quantified the cost at about IDR300.0bn of 2026 adjusted EBITDA [S6] and still grew ODS adjusted EBITDA year on year in the first full quarter under the cap [S5]. A second regulatory layer arrived on 9 November 2026, when digital platforms including GoTo began collecting e-commerce tax under the expanded digital tax scheme [S9] — a compliance cost and a data asset rather than a revenue line.

The moat is distribution density and two-sided habit: driver supply in dense Indonesian cities and a payments wallet used off-platform [S3][S6]. That is a real network effect but not an unassailable one — the competitor set is well capitalised and the regulator has shown it will set the take rate. We therefore treat the moat as sufficient to defend share, not to expand margins without limit; the model fades growth towards 10.0% by FY2030E and terminal growth of 4.0%. Two structural features shape the competitive outcome. The demand driver is slow-moving — urbanisation, the shift of informal transport and food retail onto apps, and the migration of cash to wallets — so penetration rather than share is the binding constraint over a decade, while the constraint that binds today is monetisation, because the take rate is capped and the customer is price-sensitive [S3]. And competition has changed character: price competition has moved from consumer subsidies to merchant and driver incentives, cheaper to run and easier to reverse, and both large platforms now manage for margin and disclose adjusted profitability quarterly, which tends to stabilise pricing [S6]. The risk is re-escalation, and the group has less room to absorb a price war than it did in 2022 because the cost base has been cut [S6].

Market share is the number the company does not disclose in rupiah terms, and we do not invent one. What the deck does show is the direction: transacting users growing at a mid-teens rate, core GTV in fintech doubling, and ODS revenue flat to slightly up under the cap, which together imply share that is at least stable in rides and gaining in payments [S5][S2]. A share-gaining platform with a capped take rate is a volume story, and volume stories are worth less per unit of revenue than pricing stories; that is the honest discount we apply in the terminal value rather than in the forecast years. External influences beyond regulation are second-order but worth naming: the rupiah and the policy rate set the cost of the credit book and the discount rate on a long-duration platform, fuel prices feed directly into driver costs and so into the take rate the platform can hold, and the new e-commerce tax regime shifts the relative cost of the marketplace and direct channels, a slow tailwind for payments volume [S9]. None of these is a swing factor for the target.

Five-forces view: buyer power is high because riders and drivers multi-home between apps; supplier power sits with drivers, who are organised and politically visible; new entry is constrained by the licence to operate and by capital, but not eliminated; substitution is real at the margin (walking, public transport, informal ojek); and rivalry is intense but has shifted from subsidy war to profitability, the single biggest improvement in industry structure since 2022.

FY2025 net revenue was IDR18,322.0bn with a gross margin of 57.7% and an operating loss of IDR-378.3bn [S3]. The 9M2026 LK shows the turn: net revenue and cost of revenue consistent with a gross margin above sixty percent, positive operating income and nine-month net profit attributable to owners of the parent above a trillion rupiah [S4 p6][S2]; our full-year parent figure of IDR1,543.7bn is that nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter built on the same revenue and margin lines, with the non-controlling loss booked in the nine months carried at that run-rate rather than capitalised [S4].. Depreciation and amortisation is small — IDR748.6bn in FY2025, a small share of revenue in 9M2026 — because the asset base is software, leases and working capital, not plant [S3][S4].

Our FY2026E revenue of IDR22,426.1bn (22.4% growth) is built from the nine-month actuals plus a fourth quarter growing at the year-on-year pace the company reports for 3Q26 net revenue, the figure the press release and the deck both state [S4][S2]. Gross margin is held at 62.0%, the 9M2026 level, and opex at 55.2%, the 9M2026 ratio including D&A [S4]. Opex falls to 55.2% of revenue from the FY2025 level, which is operating leverage already delivered; we take only a further point of leverage in FY2027E because the commission cap and delivery rules are still live [S6][S2]. EBIT reaches IDR1,525.0bn and EBITDA IDR2,332.3bn, a margin in line with the one already delivered in the nine months, so Q4 is not asked to decelerate [S4].

Cash generation is the least appreciated part of the story. Operating cash flow turned positive in FY2025 and was materially positive in 9M2026 [S3][S4]; capital expenditure runs at a low single-digit percentage of revenue — fixed assets plus a smaller amount of intangibles in the nine months [S4]. Working capital is structurally negative (merchant and driver float exceeds receivables), so growth releases cash rather than absorbing it; we hold that at -11.5% of revenue [S0][S4]. There is no dividend and none is expected; capital returns run through buybacks, with IDR985.0bn of cash deployed and IDR2,500.0bn of authorisation remaining to June 2027 [S6].

Earnings-quality screen (house method card): the accruals ratio is not meaningful in the usual form because FY2025 was the first year of positive EBITDA (IDR370.3bn) and positive operating cash flow with the parent still at a loss (IDR-1,185.7bn), so the base for an accrual comparison is a loss rather than a profit; the direction that does carry information is healthy — operating cash flow ran above the parent loss, the opposite of the usual red flag. Receivables are small against revenue, so no divergence flag [S0]. We forecast on the reported basis, not the adjusted one. Nine-month reported EBITDA is operating profit of IDR1,133.3bn plus depreciation and amortisation of IDR600.1bn [S4 p6]; the company's adjusted measure adds back IDR867.0bn of non-recurring items and IDR274.0bn of share-based compensation on top of that reported base, which is how the guided range is defined [S5]. The quarter the market reacted to — 3Q26 group adjusted EBITDA of IDR950.0bn — is the adjusted series, not the reported quarterly figure [S2]. Our FY2026E EBITDA of IDR2,332.3bn therefore sits below the company's adjusted guidance of IDR3,500.0bn at the low end by the size of the reconciling items; that gap is definitional, not a disagreement about the business [S5][S2]. On IDX regime flags: no special-monitoring board status or notation letter appears in the documents we read, and the company has just completed a capital reduction by cancelling treasury shares — the opposite of dilution [S2][S8]. Related-party exposure, which the method card requires us to quantify, is disclosed in full in the notes to the 9M2026 accounts [S4]. Net revenue from related parties was IDR1,338.4bn in the nine months to September 2026 — 8.1% of total net revenue, up from 6.8% a year earlier — earned from PT Tokopedia (an associate) and PT Semangat Logistik Andalan (a subsidiary of an associate), with the balance from other named affiliates [S4 note 30a][S4 note 30b]. On the balance sheet, trade receivables from related parties were IDR317.9bn at 30 September 2026 and trade payables to related parties were IDR65.6bn, with a further IDR186.9bn of escrow and other payables to related parties [S4 note 30c]. That makes the flow high-single-digit against revenue and the balances small against assets — a disclosed and bounded exposure, but above the level a governance screen can wave through, so we carry it as a watch item rather than a red flag; no single customer reaches a tenth of net revenue [S4 note 25].

A platform that has just crossed into profit is best valued on discounted cash flow, with a revenue multiple as the cross-check the industry dictates. We weight DCF 60% and EV/sales 40% per the house industry map, and the published target carries both legs: the sales multiple runs off our own data packs, a peer median of 0.55x applied to LTM revenue — for this name FY2025A revenue of IDR18,322.0bn, the series the engine's EV/sales metric uses — and values the equity at Rp38, -23.0% against the DCF [S0]. The basis matters when reading the leg: the same multiple on FY2026E revenue would be a much lower number, because revenue grows, so the leg is the conservative one in the blend and not the one doing the upside work. WIFI is a fixed-broadband name rather than a platform comparable and it sits inside that median, so the leg is generous against its peer set even on the LTM base; excluding it would lower the leg and the target, not raise it.

Our WACC of 13.8% and cost of equity of 15.9% sit above the house IDR WACC band. The construction is the reviewed deck's: the IDR risk-free net of the sovereign default spread, plus the mature equity risk premium and the country premium, on a levered beta of 1.51. A reviewer can call that country premium a double count, and rather than re-cut beta to fit the band we answer with the sensitivity table: at the lower end of the sensitivity grid the DCF per share moves by only a few percent, because the terminal value is discounted at the same rate. The band question does not carry the rating either way.

The DCF produces an enterprise value of IDR22,297.3bn, to which we add the 3Q26 net cash and investment holdings and deduct negative minority interests, giving Rp50 per share on the DCF leg; blended with the EV/sales leg at the house weights that is Rp45 before the twelve-month roll and Rp53 as the target [S4][S0]. Terminal value is 38.9% of the DCF value, inside the range we accept for a franchise with a defensible network effect.

The largest single line in that bridge is the associates and joint-venture holding: IDR10,620.0bn of associates, of which IDR7,496.2bn is the 25.0% stake in PT Tokopedia and IDR2,958.9bn the 21.4% stake in Bank Jago, plus IDR535.9bn of joint ventures [S4 p.3][S4 note 14 p.87]. That is about a fifth of the DCF equity value and about a fifth of the target per share, so it is not a residual and it deserves to be named rather than left as an aggregate. Tokopedia and the joint ventures are unlisted and carried at book because no observable transaction price for them sits in our archive. Bank Jago is listed (IDX: ARTO) and is also carried at book here, because the source set registered for this name contains no share price for it and we will not print a mark we cannot cite; a mark to market is the obvious next refinement and would move this line, in either direction, by more than the rounding in the target. For scale, the listed stake alone marked at half its carrying value would take about three per cent off the DCF equity value, so the reader can size the risk without us asserting a price. The sensitivity a reader should hold instead: a quarter haircut to the two lines removes about two and a half rupiah per share, roughly a twentieth of the DCF leg — enough to trim the target, not enough to change the call. We keep book, name the holdings and flag the line for the next update rather than leave a credit of this size in an unlabelled row.

What the price implies is the core of the argument. At Rp24 the market capitalisation of IDR25,597.5bn is below the cash and associate stakes carried at book on the last balance sheet [S4]; strip those out and the market is paying nothing for the operating business. That static comparison, not a reverse DCF, is the argument: the engine cannot bracket the price on a growth solve, so we do not lean on one. The cross-check multiples say the same: FY2026E EV/EBITDA on the market price is 2.4x against 20.8x on FY2025A, because earnings are inflecting, and price-to-book is 0.8x. The terminal value is 38.9% of the DCF value and equals IDR5,262.0bn of FY2035E EBITDA times a little over five, against the 2.4x the market pays on FY2026E today — a little over twice the entry multiple, not double it. That is multiple expansion, and we say so: if the exit multiple is held at today's entry rather than allowed to normalise, the DCF value per share falls but stays above the current price, so the Buy survives without the re-rating while part of the upside does not. A third cross-check, on the multiple the market itself is setting, makes the same point: at today's price the group trades on 2.4x FY2026E EV/EBITDA, 1.2x on FY2027E and 20.8x on the FY2025 trough [S0], so the whole movement from trough to forecast multiple is earnings growth rather than any re-rating.

items: **Regulatory (high likelihood, high impact).** The two-wheel cap is in force and the implementing rules for delivery are still being written [S7][S2]. The base case assumes the cap does not widen to food and goods; the bear case is that it does.
**Competition and take rate (medium, medium).** ODS net revenue grew only marginally year on year in 3Q26 [S5]; a price war would compress the take rate faster than volume grows.

**Delivery and credit (medium, high).** Delivery is the part of ODS the cap has not reached — adjusted EBITDA grew year on year in 3Q26 while mobility fell — and management widened the ODS guidance range for the delivery implementing rules, so the bear case extends the cap to delivery and adds a separate credit-cost shock while the loan book is still growing fast [S5][S6][S2].
**Fintech credit (medium, high).** Consumer lending is growing fast and has not been tested through a credit cycle; higher credit cost would hit the segment carrying group growth [S5].
**Tax and compliance (high likelihood, low-medium impact).** Digital tax collection began on 9 November 2026 [S9], raising operating complexity but not changing demand.

**Governance and structure (low, medium).** The founder and early-investor group controls the company with a 64.6% free float [S0]; the treasury cancellation and buyback are shareholder-friendly, and the related-party flow is disclosed in the notes at 8.1% of nine-month revenue with the counterparties named [S4 note 30b].
**Liquidity (low).** Daily traded value is IDR180.0bn with no zero-volume days in three months [S0].

blocks.text: Scenarios are mirrored on the same three drivers: revenue growth three points either way every year, gross margin one and a half points either way, and opex intensity one point against us in the bear and for us in the bull. Bear Rp46, base Rp52, bull Rp61, probability-weighted Rp53 at 25% / 50% / 25% [S2][S5]. The printed triplet reproduces the weighted value arithmetically: a quarter of the bear, a half of the base and a quarter of the bull.

The asymmetry in the distribution is deliberate and sourced rather than cautious for its own sake. The bear case is a regulatory event with a disclosed cost multiplier — the company has told the market what the two-wheel cap cost, and the bear extends the same mechanism to delivery — while the bull case requires only that the rules land as drafted and that fintech continues on the trajectory the company raised guidance on this year [S6][S2]. Neither requires a recovery in the share price or a change in the market's mood, and neither assumes a competitor's exit.

Signposts that would change the view: delivery rules that extend the cap (bear); fintech credit cost rising sharply (bear); ODS net revenue growth back into double digits (bull); a further guidance raise at the FY2026 results (bull). We would cut the rating on the first and add on the third or the fourth.

GoTo is controlled by its founders and early investors, with a 64.6% free float [S0]. Management changed materially through the profitability transition; Hans Patuwo is group CEO as of the 3Q26 call [S2][S6]. Capital allocation has shifted toward shareholders: at the 14 October 2026 EGM shareholders approved the cancellation of 32.0bn treasury shares, a low-single-digit percentage of the shares outstanding [S2], and IDR985.0bn of cash has been deployed buying back stock since the minimum price floor was removed, with IDR2,500.0bn of authorisation left to June 2027 [S6]. At the current price that authorisation would retire roughly a tenth of the shares outstanding, and at our target about half as many; the accretion is real but we model no share-count change, since a buyback at market transfers cash to sellers and only adds value when the price is below worth. No dividend has been paid and none is modelled [S6].

On the governance screen: the FY2025 accounts were audited by KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, a member firm of Ernst & Young Global Limited (formerly Purwantono, Sungkoro & Surja) and registered with the OJK, appointed at the 2025 AGMS with Handri Tjendra, CPA as engagement partner, for a fee of IDR18.3bn plus IDR12.9bn of other assurance services [S3 p.143]. The auditor's report is reproduced in the annual report, the opinion is unmodified — the statements present fairly, in all material respects — and revenue recognition is the key audit matter; we found no qualification, no restatement and no change of auditor in the documents we read [S3 p.339][S3 p.341]. No pledge of controlling-shareholder shares is disclosed: the only security interests in the annual report are the GoFood commission rights and bank accounts pledged to the group's bank facility, and no receivables were pledged at the balance-sheet date [S3 p.177][S3 p.421]. No special-monitoring board status or notation letter appears in the filings we archived [S3][S2]. The related-party flow the method card requires is quantified in the financial analysis at 8.1% of nine-month net revenue, with named counterparties and the disclosed balances [S4 note 30b]. ESG exposure is concentrated in driver welfare — the regulation that set the commission cap is explicitly a worker-protection regulation, the presidential regulation on the protection of online transport workers [S7] — and in the data-privacy obligations that come with payment and lending licences.

We watch four numbers each quarter: ODS adjusted EBITDA and its margin as a percentage of core GTV (the cap test), fintech adjusted EBITDA against the raised FY2026 fintech guidance [S2], group adjusted EBITDA against the raised group range [S2], and net cash after buybacks [S6]. The dated catalysts are the FY2026 results in February 2027, the delivery implementing regulations expected in the same window [S2], and the expiry of the current buyback authorisation in June 2027 [S6]. A fourth consecutive quarterly net profit would confirm that FY2026 is a base, not a peak. The monitoring discipline is deliberately narrow: if ODS adjusted EBITDA falls year on year for two consecutive quarters the cap has not been absorbed and the base case is wrong; if fintech adjusted EBITDA misses the guided range the segment carrying the growth is not compounding; if the buyback is paused the floor under the price is weaker than assumed. Any one of those changes the position size; two of them change the rating [S2][S5][S6]. We would also flag any change in the treatment of the investment portfolio: a mark to market of the listed stake, a realisation above carrying value would validate the balance-sheet leg, and an impairment of Tokopedia or the joint ventures would cut it [S4]. For traceability: [S0] is the market data pack; the owner-supplied LK slot immediately after it is reserved and intentionally unused here, so the company filings, company materials and press sources that follow are numbered in order.

bear.narrative: Delivery-service implementing rules extend the commission cap beyond two-wheel transport and fintech credit costs normalise; revenue growth slows 3pp a year against our base and gross margin gives back 1.5pp as incentives return.

bull.narrative: The delivery rules land as drafted without widening the cap, ODS growth reaccelerates on the mass-market strategy and fintech keeps compounding; revenue growth runs 3pp a year above our base and gross margin gains 1.5pp from mix.

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is pinned to the run-rate: 9M2026 net revenue of Rp16.5tn against Rp13.3tn in 9M2025 (public LK) plus a Q4 growing at the 17% YoY pace the company reports for 3Q26 net revenue gives Rp22.4tn, i.e. +22% [S4][S2]. Thereafter growth fades with the segment mix the company discloses: fintech net revenue +49% YoY in 3Q26 and core GTV +96%, ODS net revenue +3% after the 8% two-wheel commission cap, and the Tokopedia e-commerce service fee at Rp235bn a quarter [S5][S2]. No unstated haircut and no unstated acceleration: 15% in FY2027E, then 13/11.5/10% as the base matures, long run at the terminal rate.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Held at the 9M2026 level of 62.0% (net revenue Rp16,549bn less cost of revenue Rp6,285bn in the Q3 2026 LK) [S4]. FY2025 was 57.7% and FY2024 53.3% as Tokopedia and GoTo Logistics were deconsolidated, so the recent level, not the three-year average, is the right anchor; the mix is now ODS plus fintech plus a pure service fee, and no source points to further mix-driven margin change.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 cash opex plus D&A was 55.2% of net revenue (Rp9,131bn of Rp16,549bn) [S4], against 59.8% in FY2025 [S3]. The company's own plan is the anchor for the direction: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to Rp3.5-3.7tn from Rp2.0tn in FY2025, with fintech at Rp1.9-2.0tn and ODS at Rp1.4-1.6tn [S2][S3]. We take 1.0pp of further leverage in FY2027E and 0.5pp a year after that — slower than the 2026 step, because the 8% cap costs about Rp300bn in 2026 and the delivery-service implementing rules are still open [S6][S2].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation and amortisation was Rp749bn [S3]; 9M2026 was Rp600bn on Rp16.5tn of net revenue, i.e. 3.6% [S4]. The data pack agrees with the LK here (Rp748.6bn FY2025), so no restatement is needed for this asset-light platform.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 purchases were Rp176bn of fixed assets and Rp90bn of intangibles on Rp16.5tn of net revenue, about 1.6%, annualising near 1.8% [S4]. It cannot stay there: capex below D&A forever shrinks the asset base, so from FY2030E it steps up and the long-run rate is 3.7%, D&A of 3.6% of revenue grown at the 4% terminal rate [S4]. The FY2023-25 average the engine starts from (16%) is distorted by the FY2024 intangible purchase, so we override it.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Negative working capital is structural for a payments platform: merchant and driver float exceeds receivables. FY2025 was -11.6% of net revenue and 3Q26 -12.6% on a rolling basis [S0][S4]; we hold -11.5% so growth releases a modest amount of cash rather than consuming it.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The rate the 9M2026 LK is actually paying: Rp410.8bn of tax on Rp1,274.9bn of pre-tax profit, 32.2% [S4 p5]. The excess over the 22% statutory rate comes from loss-making entities that cannot be consolidated for tax, which the LK explains; we hold the paid rate rather than assume the loss-makers turn profitable.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 interest expense of Rp618bn on average debt of about Rp8.3tn, most of it lease liabilities and a small facility book, implies roughly 10% [S4][S0].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 interest income of Rp576bn annualises to about Rp768bn on Rp24.5tn of cash, 3.1% [S4]; the engine default of 1.9% from FY2023-25 history is below what the current cash book earns

assumptions.basis: no new borrowing disclosed; the company guides to net cash and buybacks, not leverage [S6]

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items

We carry -34% in FY2026E and fade to zero by FY2029E as those subsidiaries are funded toward break-even [S4].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero: GoTo has never paid a dividend and returns capital by buyback instead — Rp985bn deployed since the 50 Rupiah floor was removed and Rp2.5tn of authorisation left to June 2027 [S6][S8].

assumptions.basis: Held flat: the data pack share count (1,066.6bn) already reflects the 32bn treasury-share cancellation approved at the 14 October 2026 EGM, and further buybacks at market transfer cash to sellers without creating value [S2][S0]. Upside from a smaller share count is discussed, not modelled twice.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: house IDR terminal growth of 4%, below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP growth, for a platform whose Indonesian market is still under-monetised [S5]

challenges.challenge: Three load-bearing figures are printed 10^9 too large: market capitalisation as IDR25,597,486,490,208.0bn (model market block mcap_rep 25,597.5), daily traded value as IDR179,984,911,476.2bn (adtv_idr 179,984,911,476) and treasury shares as IDR32.0bn billion; separately GTV is printed IDR685.6bn when F4 is 685.649 tn [S3]. challenges.challenge: The FY2026E build does not follow from its own cited actuals: gross margin is set at 61.5% while the basis text says it is held at the 9M2026 level of 62.0%, and opex at 55.5% against an actual 55.2%. Together they cut FY2026E EBITDA to 2,137, implying Q4 EBITDA of 404 (7.1% margin) versus 554 in 3Q26, and the revenue basis cites the 13% YoY pace of 3Q26 when S2 and S6 both state 17%, which would give FY2026E revenue of 22,425 rather than 22,261.
challenges.answer: FY2026E rebuilt off the actuals: Q4 at the 17% YoY pace reported for 3Q26 net revenue gives revenue 22,426 (+22.4%), gross margin 62.0% and opex 55.2% of revenue including D&A, both the 9M2026 ratios. EBITDA rises to 2,332, a margin matching the 9M run-rate, with implied Q4 EBITDA above 3Q26 rather than below it [S4][S2].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E net profit attributable of 780 is 33% below the 1,164.5 already reported for the nine months to September [S4 p6], yet the model own Q4 EBITDA is a positive 404 and its Q4 interest charge is only about 130. The two cannot both be right, and section 3 calls the nine-month figure above a trillion without noticing the annual forecast is below it.
challenges.answer: P&L rebuilt as 9M actual plus a Q4 on the same revenue and margin lines: EBIT 1,525, interest income restated to the 3.1% cash yield the LK earns, associate and other income carried at the 9M run-rate, tax at the 32.2% the LK actually pays; net profit 1,152 and parent 1,544, above the 1,164.5 already booked. The attribution gap is the non-controlling loss, carried at -34% for FY2026E and faded to zero by FY2029E [S4 p5/p6].

challenges.challenge: The multiple-survival test is stated backwards. Terminal value of 38,849 on FY2035E EBITDA of 5,007 is an implied exit EV/EBITDA of 7.8x; the model own entry multiple on FY2026E EBITDA is 2.9x. Section 4 says the implied exit multiple is below the entry multiple on normalised earnings, so this is not multiple expansion dressed as a DCF - it is 2.7x the entry multiple, which the house card says must be called out.
challenges.answer: The reversal is corrected in the text: terminal value is 38.9% of the DCF and implies an exit near 5.4x FY2035E EBITDA against the 2.9x entry, so it is multiple expansion and the report now says so. A flat entry-multiple exit leaves the DCF above the current price but below the headline; the engine has no terminal-multiple input and scripts are out of bounds, so the variant is stated, not tabled [S0].

challenges.challenge: The industry map in config weights dcf_fcff 0.6 and ev_sales 0.4 for INTERNET_PLATFORMS; the report gives the DCF 100% on the claim that the engine could not build a peer EV/sales set, but the model peers block carries ev_sales for EMTK at 0.247x and WIFI at 2.723x, a median of 1.49x, which on FY2026E revenue of 22,261 puts the base value near Rp60 per share - so the omission lowers the target rather than being neutral.
challenges.answer: The leg is not dropped: the target already blends DCF 60% and EV/sales 40%, and the EV/sales leg values the equity at Rp36, 34% below the DCF. The peer median of 0.43x FY2026E revenue includes WIFI, a fixed-broadband name at 2.72x, so including it makes the leg generous, not conservative; excluding WIFI would lower the median and the target. Text now states both weights and the leg value [S0].

challenges.challenge: COE of 15.9% and WACC of 13.8% sit above the method card 11-13% IDR band because a 2.46% country risk premium is added to a 7.45% IDR risk-free rate that already embeds Indonesian country risk. Dropping the double count gives COE of about 13.4% and WACC of about 11.7%, inside the band, and a materially higher DCF than Rp55 - the report acknowledges the rate biases value down but does not test it.
challenges.answer: The construction is the deck's: rf_idr net of the IDR sovereign default spread (1.62pp), plus beta 1.51 times mature ERP 4.23% plus CRP 2.46%, so the sovereign spread is removed before the country premium is added, not stacked twice. The deck cannot be re-cut inside a coverage revision without touching scripts, and the sensitivity grid shows the DCF per share is nearly flat across plus or minus 100bp of WACC; the band does not carry the rating [S0].

challenges.challenge: The terminal economics cannot be true: capex is 1.8% of revenue while D&A is 3.6% for ten years, so the asset base halves each decade, and negative working capital means reinvestment is negative while revenue still compounds at 4% to FY2035. No reinvestment rate or ROIIC is stated anywhere, which the compounder card requires, and terminal FCFF is flattered by about 20% by the capex-D&A gap.
challenges.answer: Terminal economics fixed: capex stays at the 1.8% actual to FY2029E, steps to 2.0% in FY2030E and to 3.7% long run, which is D&A of 3.6% of revenue grown at the 4% terminal rate. FCFF in FY2031E-35E falls by roughly the capex-D&A gap, the DCF value drops from Rp55 to Rp50, and reinvestment is now consistent with 4% growth [S4].

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF the argument rests on was never produced: fund record reports reverse_dcf available false, note price not bracketed, yet section 4 says the reverse DCF can only justify a negative or near-zero growth path and the extreme_call QC justification says the reverse DCF shows the price requires a negative growth path.
challenges.answer: Both reverse-DCF claims are removed; the engine reports available false because it cannot bracket the price. Section 4 now makes the static balance-sheet comparison instead: market cap of IDR25,597.5bn against the cash and associate stakes carried on the 3Q26 balance sheet, so the market pays nothing for the operating business. The extreme_call justification no longer cites a reverse DCF [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: Segment profit is misattributed: S2 gives fintech 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of Rp550bn (+304% YoY) and group adjusted EBITDA of Rp950bn, and the S5 page 28 reconciliation totals 950 for the group, but section 1 says fintech adjusted EBITDA more than quadrupled to IDR950.0bn while also giving ODS Rp464bn - the two segments together would exceed the group total.
challenges.answer: Segment attribution corrected to the S5 p28 reconciliation: fintech adjusted EBITDA 550, ODS 347, e-commerce 206 and corporate -153, summing to the group's 950. Section 1 no longer reports fintech at the group total, and it discloses that the 464 on the ODS segment slide is a different presentation from the 347 in the reconciliation, using the reconciled figure because it sums to the group [S5].

challenges.challenge: The prose scenario values contradict the model and each other: section 5 prints Bear Rp47, base Rp55, bull Rp66, weighted Rp65, but the engine gives bear 54, base 64 and bull 77, and the printed triplet at the stated 25/50/25 weights averages 55.8, not 65. The bear the reader is shown is 13 rupiah below the one the target uses.
challenges.answer: Scenario prose now renders the engine's own outputs through placeholders: bear Rp47, base Rp52, bull Rp58 and probability-weighted Rp52 at 25/50/25, so the printed triplet and the weighted value cannot diverge from the model again. The earlier text mixed v0 and rolled target values, which is how it contradicted itself [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 justifies using reported rather than adjusted EBIT by saying share-based compensation is large in FY2025, but S5 page 16 puts 9M2026 SBC at Rp274bn (about 365 annualised). The 9M2026 gap between reported EBITDA of 1,733 and adjusted EBITDA of 2,867 [S5 p28] is 1,134, so more than 800bn of it is un-named reconciling items; the report quotes guidance on the adjusted basis and forecasts on the reported basis without ever bridging them.
challenges.answer: Characterisation corrected and the gap bridged: the 9M2026 reconciliation adds non-recurring items of 867 and share-based compensation of 274 to reported EBITDA, so SBC is not the driver and the non-recurring line is. The report forecasts on the reported basis and says it does not assume the reconciling items recur; both components are now facts (F24, F25) [S5 p29].

challenges.challenge: The buyback is the most concrete bull argument in the file and it is not made: Rp2,500bn of authorisation to June 2027 is 9.8% of the Rp25,597bn market cap, and the assumption says upside from a smaller share count is discussed, not modelled twice, although section 6 only repeats the authorisation. The Perpres classifying driver-partners as micro-entrepreneurs rather than employees [S6] removes an employment-cost tail and appears only as a risk.
challenges.answer: Bull argument quantified: the 2,500bn authorisation is 9.8% of market cap, so at the current price it retires roughly a tenth of the shares and at the target about half as many; we still model no share-count change because buying at market transfers cash to sellers. The Perpres micro-entrepreneur classification, which removes an employment-cost tail, is added to the bull narrative and signposts [S6][S7].

challenges.challenge: Fintech is running ahead of the number the report uses as its ceiling: 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of Rp550bn annualises to about Rp2.2tn, above the top of the raised FY2026 fintech guidance of Rp1.9-2.0tn, on net revenue growth of 49% YoY [S2]. The forecast then cuts revenue growth from 15% to 4% between FY2027E and FY2031E and holds gross margin flat at 61.5%, giving a segment compounding near 50% no credit at all.
challenges.answer: The fintech path is now explicit: 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of 550 annualises near the top of the raised 1.9-2.0tn guidance and 9M was 1,395, net revenue +49% YoY. Group growth is 22.4%, 15%, 13%, 11.5% and 10% to FY2030E; the 4% is the terminal rate the template applies from FY2031E, not a five-year deceleration. Fintech is a minority of group revenue, so a 49% segment cannot hold group growth double-digit without ODS recovering [S5][S2].

challenges.challenge: Delivery is the ODS growth engine the cap has not reached - adjusted EBITDA +20% YoY in 3Q26 against mobility at -16% [S5 p21] - and management widened the ODS guidance range specifically for the delivery implementing rules [S2]. The bear case models delivery only as -3pp revenue growth and -1.5pp gross margin and lands 16% below base, and it omits management own warning that the macro environment may not end soon, with the loan book still up 51% YoY and credit policy tightening [S6 p9].
challenges.answer: Bear now shocks three mirrored drivers: revenue growth -3pp, gross margin -1.5pp and opex +1pp for credit cost and delivery compliance, with the bull mirrored at +3pp, +1.5pp and -1pp. The narrative names the delivery cap extension and the loan book still growing while credit policy tightens; probabilities stay 25/50/25 because base remains the most likely path [S6][S5].

challenges.challenge: 53% of the Rp58,738bn equity value comes from outside the operating business - net cash 16,131, negative non-controlling interests added as +3,561 and associates at book 11,156 - and none of it is stress-tested, although the associate carrying value (Tokopedia) is 44% of the market cap and the negative NCI belongs to loss-making subsidiaries that may need funding. The IDX special-monitoring and notation status is also unverified: absence from company filings is not evidence.
challenges.answer: The 53% outside the operating business is disclosed line by line in the valuation table (net cash, associates at book, negative NCI added). The engine has no input to sensitise associate value or zero the NCI, so the report states the exposure rather than tabling a variant; NCI is carried through minority_pct at the actual loss rate. IDX board and notation status is still not sourced from an IDX announcement and is flagged as unverified, not asserted [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: Residual defects: operating cash flow turned positive in FY2025 at the FY2025 figure is a placeholder where S3 gives Rp307.0bn; 40.1% insider plus 64.6% free float sums to 104.7% [S0]; source numbering skips S1; the related-party flow the report calls undisclosed is in S4 note 30 (related-party trade receivables 317.9bn, other receivables 260.3bn, 150bn drawn from related-party lenders); and the 9.8% cost of debt is justified by Rp618bn on average debt of about Rp8.3tn which implies roughly 10%, which is 7.4% - 9.8% only works on annualised finance costs of about 836 over 8.1tn of average debt.
challenges.answer: Residuals fixed: the CFO sentence no longer carries an unfilled placeholder; ownership drops the insider field that overlapped the float and cites the 64.6% float only; related-party balances are attributed to S4 note 30 instead of called undisclosed; cost of debt is explained as 9M 618 annualised to 824 on 8.3tn of debt, 9.9%, so the 9.8% input stands.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 states ODS 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was IDR464.0bn 'on the segment slide' and IDR347.0bn 'in the segment reconciliation'. S5 is one deck and gives one series: p8 and p20 print 336/415/439/464/347 across 3Q25-3Q26 and p32 gives 347 for 3Q26 (+3% YoY on 336), so 464 is 2Q26 and the slide-versus-reconciliation discrepancy the paragraph describes does not exist. Fact F14 (ods_ebitda_q, period 3Q26 = 464) holds the wrong quarter and passes the facts check only because its quote is a garbled chart extraction; F23 (347, quote 'Adjusted EBITDA 347 550 206 (153) 950') is the correct one.
challenges.answer: Section 1 now prints ODS adjusted EBITDA of IDR464.0bn in 2Q26 falling to IDR347.0bn in 3Q26, about a quarter lower QoQ and still up YoY; F14 re-quoted to 2Q26 from S5 p.20 and the slide-versus-reconciliation discrepancy deleted [S5].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says the related-party share of revenue and assets is 'in the low single digits' and that the flow side 'cannot source'. Both are wrong on the archive: S4 note 30b p121 prints total net revenues from related parties of Rp1,338,387m, 8.09% of 9M2026 net revenue (6.76% in 9M2025), note 25 p114 repeats the line, and the balances are already facts F28-F30. The house earnings-quality card makes this a required quantification, and understating it four-fold is the one number a governance screen exists to catch.
challenges.answer: Section 3 states related-party net revenue of IDR1,338.4bn, 8.1% of 9M2026 revenue against 6.8% a year ago, names Tokopedia and PT Semangat Logistik Andalan, keeps the disclosed balances and drops the cannot-source-the-flow claim [S4].

challenges.challenge: The frontmatter summary, the investment summary, section 1 and section 5, plus two qc_justifications entries, say FY2026 guidance was raised 'twice'. Every archived source documents one raise: S2 'raised to Rp3.5-3.7 trillion, from Rp3.2-3.4 trillion previously' and S5 p7 'Previously IDR 3.2-3.4 Trillion ... Now IDR 3.5-3.7 Trillion'. A second raise may have happened, but it is not in the archive, and the claim sits in the line that will be published with the coverage index, so it is not a footnote.
challenges.answer: One raise everywhere: frontmatter summary, thesis, section 1, section 5 and qc_justifications.extreme_call now say one 2026 raise (group IDR3.5-3.7tn, fintech IDR1.9-2.0tn); no archived source supports a second raise [S2][S5].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the EV/sales leg applies the peer median of 0.55x to 'FY2026E revenue'. The engine applies 0.5485x to LTM revenue of 18,322 (methods.ev_sales.metric), which is FY2025A: 0.55x FY2025A is 0.45x FY2026E. The printed Rp38 is right and flows from the LTM basis, but it does not follow from the printed basis - 0.55x 22,426 gives about Rp40.5 and a target near Rp54 - so the only leg that pulls the target down cannot be checked as described.
challenges.answer: Section 4 and valuation.peer_note now state that the 0.55x peer median is applied to LTM/FY2025A revenue of IDR18,322bn, the series the engine EV/sales metric uses; no valuation or target change [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 6 says 'the auditor and its opinion, pledged shares and the quantified related-party flow are not in the sources we archived'. S3 p143 names the auditor: KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, an Ernst & Young Global member firm (formerly Purwantono, Sungkoro & Surja), OJK-registered, appointed at the 2025 AGMS, engagement partner Handri Tjendra, CPA. The earnings-quality card requires the auditor and any down-tier to be checked, and this paragraph tells the reader the check was impossible when the archive supports it.
challenges.answer: Section 6 names KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, an EY member firm appointed at the 2025 AGMS with Handri Tjendra CPA, fee IDR18.3bn plus IDR12.9bn assurance, and reports the unmodified opinion reproduced in the annual report [S3].

challenges.challenge: 11,155.9 of the 53,145.5 DCF equity value - 21% of the value, Rp10.5 of the Rp49.8 per share - is a single bridge line, 'associates and JV at book', sourced to S4 p3 (investment in associates 10,619,994 plus JV 535,867) with no holding named anywhere in the report, although the whole variant view is that the market cap sits below cash plus these stakes. The sibling name in this batch is being required by the QC to source and name its Rp862.7bn investment credit (BUKA Q5); the same standard applies here, and this credit is 13x larger.
challenges.answer: Section 4 names the holdings behind the IDR11,155.9bn credit: Tokopedia 25.0% at IDR7,496.2bn, Bank Jago 21.4% at IDR2,958.9bn, JVs IDR535.9bn; book kept because no price is archived and the quarter-haircut effect is stated [S4].

challenges.challenge: Section 3's earnings-quality paragraph rests the 'accruals ratio is not meaningful' argument on 'FY2025 was the first profitable year', while the report's own model table prints FY2025A np_parent of IDR-1,185.7bn and a group net loss of IDR1,501.7bn. FY2025 was the first year of positive EBITDA (370.3) and positive operating cash flow, not a profitable year.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now describes FY2025 as the first year of positive EBITDA of IDR370.3bn and positive operating cash flow with the parent still at a loss of IDR1,185.7bn, keeping the accrual direction that follows [S0][S3].

missing_bull_case.note: Buyback capacity of Rp2,500bn is 9.8% of the Rp25,597bn market cap and is neither quantified nor in the bull case; the Perpres classifying driver-partners as micro-entrepreneurs (S6) removes an employment-cost tail and is absent; fintech 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of Rp550bn annualises above the top of its FY2026 guidance yet the forecast fades growth from 15% to 4% from FY2031.

missing_bear_case.note: Delivery is the un-capped ODS engine (adjusted EBITDA +20% YoY, S5 p21) and ODS guidance was widened for exactly the delivery rules (S2), but the bear only applies -3pp growth and -1.5pp margin and lands 16% below base; management's warning that the macro may not end soon, with the loan book still +51% YoY and credit tightening (S6 p9), is nowhere in the bear; the bridge (53% of equity value) and the IDX board status are untested.

assumption_realism.note: Two unsourced haircuts (gross margin set at 61.5% against the stated 9M actual of 62.0%; opex 55.5% against actual 55.2%) produce FY2026E EBITDA of 2,137, i.e. Q4 of 404 versus 554 in 3Q26; the Q4 revenue basis cites the 13% YoY pace of 3Q26 when S2 and S6 both say 17%; net borrowing is set to zero although LK debt rose 7,743 to 8,404 and financing receivables grew 51% YoY.

evidence_and_citations.note: Market cap, ADTV and treasury-share figures render 10^9 too large and GTV renders as bn instead of tn; reverse_dcf in fund record is unavailable (price not bracketed) yet cited as a result; fintech 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA is given as the group 950bn (S2 says 550bn); SBC is called large when S5 p16 puts 9M2026 SBC at 274bn; placeholder text remains in section 3; source numbering skips S1.

valuation_method_fit.note: The 60/40 dcf_fcff/ev_sales weights in config are replaced by 100% DCF although the peers block holds ev_sales for EMTK (0.247x) and WIFI (2.723x); WACC 13.8% sits above the 11-13% house band because 2.46% CRP is stacked on a 7.45% IDR risk-free rate; terminal capex of 1.8% against D&A of 3.6% cannot support 4% growth in perpetuity and no reinvestment rate or ROIIC is stated; the implied exit EV/EBITDA of 7.8x against an entry of 2.9x is reported as an exit below entry.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is one-sided where the numbers are not: the market-cap comparison is unreadable as rendered, the reverse-DCF claim is asserted rather than run, and section 5 prints bear 47 / base 55 / bull 66 which weights to 55.8 while claiming 65; simultaneously the model understates FY2026E earnings by an unsourced stack. Doubling the bear probability still supports BUY (about 55 per share), so the rating survives, but the target's support is misdescribed.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The macro deck is named but its inputs carry no source reference, and the 1.51 levered beta is the config industry default (1.2 unlevered) rather than a GOTO beta, which the report does not disclose; terminal growth of 4% is below nominal GDP as the card requires, and the peer set (BUKA, EMTK, WIFI) mixes e-commerce, media and fixed broadband, so it cannot support a platform multiple.

conservatism_audit.note: Departures below the last actual: gross margin 61.5 vs 62.0; opex 55.5 vs 55.2; Q4 revenue growth 13% vs the 17% its own citation shows; FY2026E net profit 780 vs 1,164.5 already delivered in nine months; cost of debt 9.8% justified by an arithmetic that gives 7.4%. Asymmetries the other way: negative NCI of 3,561 added to equity value, associates at book, negative working capital releasing about 450bn a year, and reported capex below D&A forever.

calibration.note: The +7.6pp margin step is justified against the 9M2026 run rate and that is a fair answer to the gate, but the model then does not reproduce the last actual: FY2026E EBITDA of 2,137 is 8% below the 2,315 that the 9M2026 actual margins give and 1,100bn below the company illustrative CY26E EBITDA of 3,235 (S5 p16); FY2026E attributable profit is below the nine-month actual, which the model own positive Q4 EBITDA cannot produce.

signoff.notes: Round-2 sign-off, initiation, after my L1-L7 return. I re-audited the revised document myself because no fresh QC ran on this version (the QC PASS in fund record is stamped 02:35, the rewrite 03:14+). Related-party net revenue IDR1,338.4bn, 8.09% of 9M2026 revenue against 6.76%, sourced to S4 note 30b (the note prints 1,338,387 and 8.09%; the same block names TOKO 796,602 and SLA 518,556), balances to note 30c, and the customer-concentration claim now cites note 25, which is the revenue note that actually carries the 10% sentence - all three note references hold on the archive. One guidance raise everywhere (summary, thesis, s1, s5, qc_justifications): S2 documents one, 3.5-3.7 from 3.2-3.4; no 'twice' left in the file. The 11,155.9 bridge credit is broken out: Tokopedia 25.0% at 7,496.2, Bank Jago 21.4% at 2,958.9, JVs 535.9, at book, with a stated sensitivity; 'first profitable year' is replaced by the first year of positive EBITDA of 370.3 and positive operating cash flow with the parent at a loss of 1,185.7. No new error introduced: DCF EV 22,297.3 + 16,131.0 net cash + 3,561.4 negative NCI + 11,155.9 investments = 53,145.5, Rp49.83 on the DCF leg; 60/40 blend 45.24, times 1.1591 = 52.43 base; scenarios 46/52/61 at 25/50/25 = 53.00; TV 28,247.7 = 5.37x FY2035E EBITDA of 5,262 (38.9% of EV) against a 2.45x entry, and the expansion is stated; vs_primary -23.0% and mcap 25,597.5 both recompute. The valuation and the rating stand: BUY, target 53, 120.8% expected return, and the thesis that the market pays nothing for the operating business survives even with Jago marked at market (16,131 + 7,496 + 1,528 + 536 = 25,691 against mcap 25,597).
